name.en: Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED)
name.local: 国立研究開発法人日本医療研究開発機構

aka: 日本医療研究開発機構

check_size.raw: grants of up to ¥10 billion per project (Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem)

strategy.thesis: Japan's central government funding agency for medical R&D (Japan's 'NIH equivalent'), unifying budgets formerly split across MEXT/MHLW/METI. Its Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem provides matching grants to unlisted drug-development startups (non-clinical through Phase 1/2) that are co-invested in by AMED-registered/certified venture capital firms, functioning as a government risk-capital catalyst for Japanese biotech.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Runs a VC-certification scheme (41 registered VCs as of April 2026) that determines eligibility for matching-grant co-investment into preclinical/Phase 1/Phase 2 drug-development startups; also runs the iD3 Booster service advising academic drug-seed researchers on IP and R&D strategy.

summary.en: Japan's national medical-research funding agency; through its Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem it grants matching capital to biotech startups alongside AMED-certified venture capital co-investors.
summary.local: 日本の医療研究開発の司令塔機関。「創薬ベンチャーエコシステム強化事業」を通じ、認定VCと協調投資する形で創薬ベンチャーに開発資金を提供している。

sources.title: Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem / List of Registered Venture Capitals
sources.supports: program mechanism, certified VC count (41 as of April 2026)

sources.title: National Granted Programs and Public Funds for Biopharmaceutical Startups in Japan
sources.quote: the Strengthening Program is a mechanism through which AMED provides grants to unlisted biopharmaceutical startups that have drug candidates in the clinical development stage, providing up to 10 billion yen per project

verification_notes: AMED itself is a grant-making agency, not an equity investor; its investor-relevant activity is the matching-grant/certified-VC mechanism described above. Stage tagging (seed/A/B) is an approximation of 'non-clinical through Phase 2' drug-development stage, not a literal VC round mapping.

name.local: JICベンチャー・グロース・インベストメンツ株式会社

strategy.thesis: Wholly state-backed venture-growth investor operating as a subsidiary of Japan Investment Corporation (JIC, majority-owned by the Japanese government). Life sciences is one of JIC VGI's designated priority sectors (alongside deep tech and AI), with a dedicated ¥15 billion early-stage allocation, and the firm is registered as an AMED-certified venture capital for the Strengthening Program for Pharmaceutical Startup Ecosystem.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Life sciences became a formal JIC investment theme in June 2020; JIC VGI reserves a ¥15 billion early-stage allocation each for life sciences and deep tech.

summary.en: Government-owned venture-growth investment arm of Japan Investment Corporation (JIC), with a dedicated early-stage life-sciences allocation and status as an AMED-certified VC for biotech matching-grant co-investment.
summary.local: 政府系ファンド産業革新投資機構（JIC）の子会社。ライフサイエンスを重点領域の一つとし、AMED認定VCとして創薬ベンチャーへの協調投資を行う。

name.en: START — Program for Creating STart-ups from Advanced Research and Technology (JST)
name.local: 大学発新産業創出プログラム（START）

strategy.thesis: Flagship national program of the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) that pairs public R&D funding with private-sector 'business promoter' expertise to launch startups from university and national-lab research seeds, explicitly spanning bio/life-science technology fields, aiming to transition projects to private capital within roughly three years.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Uses an external 'business promoter' unit model to combine public seed funding with commercialization know-how before company creation; also runs a university/regional 'startup ecosystem' track for entrepreneurship training.

summary.en: JST's national program funding pre-startup R&D and business-promoter-led commercialization from Japanese university/national-lab research seeds, including bio and life-science fields, ahead of private-capital handoff.
summary.local: JST（科学技術振興機構）による大学発ベンチャー創出プログラム。事業プロモーターと連携し、バイオ・ライフサイエンス分野を含む研究シーズの起業前支援を行う。

name.en: INCJ, Ltd. (formerly Innovation Network Corporation of Japan / 産業革新機構)
name.local: 株式会社INCJ（旧・株式会社産業革新機構）

strategy.thesis: Japan's original government-backed 'risk money' fund (est. 2009 as Innovation Network Corporation of Japan; restructured 2018 as INCJ under new parent Japan Investment Corporation), which invested in areas private capital under-serves, including AI/bio/drug-discovery — funding cases spanning a Daiichi Sankyo-partnered muscular-dystrophy drug program, pharma venture Aqua Therapeutics, iPS-cell-derived platelet mass-production support, and vaccine maker Create Vaccine (jointly with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma).

summary.en: Japan's original state-backed innovation-investment fund (2009-2025); among its 144 total portfolio deals it backed several medical/biopharma ventures (muscular-dystrophy drug development, iPS-derived platelet manufacturing, vaccine production) before exiting all positions and being absorbed into Japan Investment Corporation (JIC) in 2025.
summary.local: 日本初の官民ファンド型投資機関（2009年設立、2025年解散・JICに吸収合併）。筋ジストロフィー治療薬開発やiPS細胞由来血小板量産、ワクチン製造など医療・バイオ分野にも出資していた。

name.en: Global Health Innovative Technology Fund (GHIT Fund)
name.local: グローバルヘルス技術振興基金（GHITファンド）

strategy.thesis: International public-private partnership co-founded and funded by the Government of Japan (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare) together with 16 Japanese pharma/diagnostics companies, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Wellcome Trust and UNDP, to fund R&D of new drugs, vaccines and diagnostics for malaria, tuberculosis and neglected tropical diseases by mobilizing Japanese industry and academia into global product-development partnerships.

aum.raw: approximately ¥29.1 billion invested cumulatively across 118 projects

summary.en: Japan-government-co-founded public-private partnership fund that has invested roughly ¥29.1 billion across 118 global-health R&D projects (drugs, vaccines, diagnostics for malaria, TB and neglected tropical diseases) with Japanese pharma companies and global partners including the Gates Foundation.
summary.local: 日本政府（外務省・厚生労働省）と国内製薬企業、ゲイツ財団等が共同設立した官民パートナーシップ基金。マラリア・結核・顧みられない熱帯病治療薬等の研究開発に累計約291億円、118案件に投資。

sources.title: Public-Private Fund Bolsters Global Partnerships in Fighting Infectious Diseases
sources.quote: an international public-private partnership between the Government of Japan (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare), 16 pharmaceutical and diagnostics companies... the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the Wellcome Trust and United Nations Development Programme

sources.title: Investment Overview | GHIT Fund

verification_notes: GHIT is a hybrid public-private structure; classified here as government-program (primary) with venture-philanthropy as secondary type given the Government of Japan is a founding funder and its mandate is R&D grant/co-funding rather than equity investment. Exact founding year not captured with a verbatim source in this pass.

name.en: DBJ Capital Co., Ltd. (Development Bank of Japan Group)

aka: DBJ Innovation Life Science Fund (former name)

strategy.thesis: Venture/growth investment subsidiary wholly owned by the Development Bank of Japan (DBJ), a majority government-owned policy financial institution. DBJ set up a dedicated Innovation Life Science Fund in March 2021 (renamed DBJ Startup Innovation Fund in November 2022) as part of its equity risk-capital mandate; DBJ Capital continues to list bio/healthcare as one of its priority sectors alongside frontier-tech and IT.

funds.name: DBJ Innovation Life Science Fund → DBJ Startup Innovation Fund

summary.en: Venture-investment arm of the Development Bank of Japan, a government-owned policy bank; set up a dedicated life-science venture fund in 2021 (since folded into a broader startup fund) as part of DBJ's public equity risk-capital supply, with bio/healthcare remaining a named focus sector.
summary.local: 日本政策投資銀行（DBJ）グループのベンチャー投資会社。2021年に「DBJイノベーション・ライフサイエンスファンド」を設置(2022年に「DBJスタートアップ・イノベーションファンド」へ改称)。バイオ・ヘルスケアは同社の重点分野の一つ。

name.local: ヘルスケア・ニューフロンティア・ファンド

strategy.thesis: Prefectural government-seeded venture fund created under Kanagawa's 'Healthcare New Frontier' policy to back startups in the 'mibyo' (pre-symptomatic/preventive health) and cutting-edge medical industries; Kanagawa Prefecture is a limited partner alongside private LPs, with GP Capital Medica Ventures selected via public tender. Japan's first healthcare-sector fund to adopt formal social-impact measurement.

aum.raw: 総額12.5億円 (approx. ¥1.25 billion total fund size)

summary.en: Kanagawa Prefecture-backed ¥1.25 billion venture fund (est. 2018) dedicated to preventive-health ('mibyo') and cutting-edge medical startups, operated by GP Capital Medica Ventures with the prefecture as an LP; the first Japanese healthcare fund to formally measure social impact.
summary.local: 神奈川県が出資する総額12.5億円のヘルスケア分野特化ベンチャーファンド（2018年設立）。未病産業・最先端医療産業のベンチャー企業を支援し、ヘルスケア分野で全国初の社会的インパクト測定を導入。
